definition: Tacit means understood or expressed without words.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word tacit. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know tacit should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: There is a tacit seating chart in the faculty lounge, and the new hire learned it by taking Hal's chair exactly once.
Implied stops short of tacit — an implied warning still rides on words somebody actually said; a tacit rule was never spoken at all.
Unthinking goes further than tacit — a tacit pact is understood by everyone it binds, while an unthinking habit runs before understanding even wakes.

Unspoken is the plain-English twin — it reports only that a thing was never said aloud. Tacit adds a second claim: everyone involved understands it and abides by it anyway. A grudge can be unspoken and known to nobody; a tacit rule is silently in force for all.

Understood means settled between people, and the settling may have happened in words long ago — a deal discussed once and never revisited. Tacit is stricter: the understanding was never put into words at all, and yet it binds everyone just the same.

Call your own fouls, but call them rarely.
